I double checked the rule book after the last thread.

Section 6.5.5 DIABLERIE
Last sentence definately is in error. It says a Blood Hunt may be
called, which as you can see is the following paragraph.

Section 6.5.6 THE BLOOD HUNT.

Messages.Author: The Fanboy
Messages.Body:
> we all know thats incorrect, Sooo... the last Sentance of 6.5.5 should
> be removed. It will eventually mean I don't have to argue myself blue
> in the face with some new player about why 6.5.6 is not optional and who
> the Referendum is required.

"May" implies either an option (you may or may not call one), or a
possibility (it may or may not be called). In this case, the word is
used in reference to the possibility.

Muaziz, Theo, and a few other vampires, as well as any vampire that's
been made an Archon, can diablerize without a possibility of a Blood
Hunt being called. In these cases, a Blood Hunt may NOT be called.
So the wording is correct.

Fanboy, using his degree in Semantics.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <3EE1E236...@mich.com>, Raille <rai...@mich.com> writes:
>As is 6.5.5 seems to allow the player to skip 6.5.6,, dropping that
>sentence remove a point of confusion and 1.4 allows it to be voided as
>needed to fit various card effects and vampire specials.

You are the one who is confused.

The Blood Hunt *is* optional. The Blood Hunt *may*, maybe, might be
called.

6.5.5 notes that the Blood Hunt may be called. 6.5.6 details how the
referendum is conducted to see if that Blood Hunt is called.

The Blood Hunt is *not* the referendum. The referendum *is* called,
save for the provisions of 1.4. The Blood Hunt *may* be called,
dependent on that referendum.

6.5.5 details the potential threat to a vampire; 6.5.6 details how you
determine if that threat is invoked.

Let me try a different tack. The Blood Hunt is a World of Darkness
way of describing how the condemned vampire is burned.

People sometimes refer to the referendum as the "Blood Hunt". This is
where the confusion comes from, I believe. May is used in 6.5.5
because whether or not the Blood Hunt happens depends on whether the
referendum is sucessful.

If the referendum is successful then there is a Blood Hunt.

If the referendum is not successful, then there is *no* Blood Hunt.

Hope this makes it clearer and not muddier...
Doug

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <3EE3632C...@mich.com>, Raille <rai...@mich.com> writes:
>Perhaps you should actually pick up the rule book and look at it.
>6.5.6 is call the Blood Hunt,

The Blood Hunt is called the Blood Hunt. 6.5.6 is sub-titled the Blood
Hunt, because it is about it.

>and according to 6.5.5 it is optional.

It, the Blood Hunt, may occur. Please not that "may" occur is not the
same as optional. If it occurs, it is not optional. If it does not
occur, it is still not optional. But it may, might, maybe occur. If
you are explaining to players that it is optional, you are only going to
confuse them. The rule book does not define it as optional.

Optional is not the same as "may be called", can occur, might happen,
maybe. This explains that it may be called, or it may not. It doesn't
dictate *how* it may be called, or *why* it may be called. So then you
read 6.5.6 which, being called Blood Hunt, is about the Blood Hunt!

So, someone actually *reading* 6.5.6 will find that it details the Blood
Hunt and how it might occur.

A player reading 6.5.6 will find:

"As stated, vampiric society condemns the act of diablerie. "

Gosh, you mean we might be going over bits of things already mentioned?
Such shocking, shocking behaviour.

"When a vampire commits diablerie, a referendum is automatically
conducted to determine if a blood hunt will be called on the
diablerist. "

So, a vampire committing diablerie will automatically cause a referendum
to be conducted, which *may* result in a blood hunt being called on
them. So the referendum -> blood hunt. referendum != blood hunt

Hence, they can even see that the Blood Hunt is not the referendum, by
*reading* the text. And the Blood Hunt may occur, but only if the
referendum passes.

What's even remotely tricky about this? A player sees a Blood Hunt may
be called in 6.5.5. A player reads 6.5.6 to find out how this may
happen.

By your bizarre logic, a player reads 1.6.3.1 and finds that a minion
*can* take an action with an action card. They can then safely ignore
the rest of the rest of the rules because it's obviously optional. Or
they can read the rest of the rules to find out how it can occur!

May. They don't know when it may occur, and when it might not occur.
So they read 6.5.6 and it tells them all about the Blood Hunt, including
when it may or may not occur! Ta-da!

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Raille wrote:

> James Coupe wrote:
>> The Blood Hunt *is* optional. The Blood Hunt *may*, maybe, might be
>> called.
>
> Perhaps you should actually pick up the rule book and look at it.
> 6.5.6 is call the Blood Hunt, and according to 6.5.5 it is optional.

6.5.6 is "The Blood Hunt" (not "Call the Blood Hunt").

The Blood Hunt may be called. [6.5.5] It is more "conditional" than
it is optional. The Blood Hunt isn't called if the referendum (which
is automatically conducted) fails. Thus the "may". It might be called.
Or it might not. Whether it is called or not depends on the outcome
of the referendum.

The referendum conducted to see if the Blood Hunt will be called is
always called after a successful diablerie. [6.5.6]

If the referendum passes, then the Blood Hunt is called. If the
referendum fails, then the Blood Hunt is not called.

> Recall that the rule book is NOT for the grognards like us, its for the
> new player. They will end up confused, and thats Not a good thing.

New players understand it just fine. Old players who have been
misusing the terms (as I have done in the past) may be confused.
If the new player learns from an old player who is misusing the terms,
the new player may be confused as well.

> Please show me in the rule book on who you determine when the blood hunt
> (6.5.6) *may* be called. And you'll see that there is Nothing there.

[6.5.6]: "When a vampire commits diablerie, a referendum is automatically

conducted to determine if a blood hunt will be called on the diablerist.

If the referendum passes, a blood hunt is called, and the diablerist is
burned."

> Dropping the last sentance of 6.5.5 does nothing to confuse the game
> play and allows you to drop right into the next rules section governing
> the Referendum and resulting blood hunt.

Leaving the last sentence of 6.5.5 does nothing to confuse the game
play and alerts the reader to the possible drawback of diablerie,
serving as a nice segue to 6.5.6.

But this is completely immaterial to the subject at hand - a rulebook
"error" rather than an error on the part of the reader.

Messages.Author: Doug
Messages.Body:
LSJ <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote in message news:<3EE38608...@white-wolf.com>...


My feeling is that the use of the word "call" in reference to the
Blood Hunt may be where the confusion comes from. The word "called"
is used as part of the standard phrasing on all political action
cards, i.e "Political Card - Worth 1 Vote. *Called* by any vampire at
+1 stealth." Because vampires "call" referenda, it is easy to
misunderstand that the Blood Hunt is another term for the referendum
called after a diablerie.

I agree that a careful reading of the text of 6.5.5 and 6.5.6
adequately explains the rules, but because the word "call" as a game
term has such a specific use, it might be better to rephrase the
statement as it relates to Blood Hunts in future rulebooks.

Doug

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Doug wrote:
> My feeling is that the use of the word "call" in reference to the
> Blood Hunt may be where the confusion comes from. The word "called"
> is used as part of the standard phrasing on all political action
> cards, i.e "Political Card - Worth 1 Vote. *Called* by any vampire at
> +1 stealth." Because vampires "call" referenda, it is easy to
> misunderstand that the Blood Hunt is another term for the referendum
> called after a diablerie.

"Call" has no specific game term - the standard English definition is
used. Blood Hunts are called (if the appropriate referendum passes).
Referendums are called (automatically in the case of diablerie, as
part of the resolution of a successful political action in other cases).
